clue.text: Hype — wholly for injecting by a doctor, we hear

indicators.note: injecting means one word is pushed inside another, here the word for 'wholly' into 'by'

parts.note: taken as written
wholly means all, completely

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is to be taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling title character of the long-running British TV series

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that all the hype is a doctor's injection sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injecting' puts ALL inside BY; 'we hear' turns WHO (the TV Doctor) into its sound, HOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy publicity or fuss, which is exactly what hype is.

clue.text: Scratches from nail point bandaged by a sister initially

indicators.note: bandaged by means the inner pieces are wrapped round by the outer ones, as a dressing wraps a wound

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means take just the opening letter of the word sister

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat-headed nail
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A nurse dresses a scrape caused by the point of a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandaged by' wraps A and S (from 'sister initially') round BRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear away a surface, so abrades means scratches as a verb.

clue.text: By which Florence Nightingale achieved recognition?

definitions.text: By which Florence Nightingale achieved recognition?

parts.words: By which Florence Nightingale achieved recognition?
parts.note: the nursing pioneer was famous as the Lady with the Lamp, so her fame came via the glow she carried on night rounds; also simply what let wounded soldiers see and recognise her

explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale nursed soldiers in the Crimean War and was known as 'the Lady with the Lamp'.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow of a lamp is the means by which she could be seen, and the image by which she became famous.

clue.text: Family doctor, not male

indicators.note: not means the word for 'male' is dropped from the longer word for a doctor

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: A patient asks for a family doctor who is a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' looks like one phrase (a GP); in fact 'Family' is the definition and 'doctor' is HOUSEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a family line or dynasty, as in the House of Windsor.

clue.text: Situation without complications for candidate for surgery?

definitions.meaning: a matter so clear it is settled at once
read literally, a patient to be cut open and sewn shut again

explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is a straightforward matter, and punningly a patient opened and closed by a surgeon.

clue.text: Instrument, one deployed in a theatre

definitions.meaning: a person used as a tool by someone else
a figure worked by strings or a hand on a small stage

explanation.definitionFit: A puppet is someone controlled by another, and also a figure moved by strings in a show.

clue.text: Yearly rise reportedly for bacteriologist

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the result is heard, not spelt

parts.note: yearly gives PA (per annum) and rise gives STIR, as in stirring from bed

explanation.surface: A scientist's annual pay increase is the subject of rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: PA (per annum, yearly) plus STIR (rise, get up) said aloud sounds like the French scientist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French scientist who founded the study of microbes and germ theory.

clue.text: Section of wall used for list of medical practitioners

definitions.meaning: a flat rectangular piece set into a wall
a register of doctors a patient may choose from, as in a GP's list

explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a flat board in a wall, and also a roster of doctors serving insured patients.

clue.text: Almost ready in operating scene for 19

indicators.note: in means the shortened word for 'ready' sits inside the rearranged letters
operating means the letters of scene are worked into a new order
almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: A surgeon is all but ready in the operating theatre to start on a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operating' rearranges SCENE to ESNCE; 'Almost' cuts SET to SE, and 'in' puts SE inside. 19 is HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its core, the heart of the matter.

clue.text: Short hallucinogenic experience, first for medical orderly

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a drug-induced hallucinatory episode

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word medical is used

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly has a brief drug trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medical orderly' looks like one phrase, a hospital porter; 'orderly' alone is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim means neat and tidy, in good order.

clue.text: Anxiety, sickly feeling without question, after one local

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'

indicators.note: without means the letter for question is removed

parts.note: queasiness is a feeling of nausea
question gives QU

explanation.surface: A patient's worry and nausea come after an unanswered query from a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without question' removes Q from QUEASINESS, and 'after' puts that behind UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasiness is a state of worry and disquiet.

clue.text: Expression briefly couched in praise for doctor

indicators.note: couched in means one piece lies inside another, as if bedded down in it

parts.note: to adulate is to praise excessively

indicators.note: briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A short compliment wrapped in flattery for a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is the verb, to tamper with. 'briefly' cuts TERM to TER, and 'couched in' puts it inside ADULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to spoil something by adding impurities, which is one sense of doctoring it.

clue.text: Doctor replaces hint of cure with new prescribed course

indicators.note: replaces with means one letter gives way to another letter in the word
replaces with means one letter gives way to another letter in the word

parts.note: to lace a drink is to doctor it with something added

indicators.note: hint of means only the opening letter of the word cure is used

explanation.surface: A doctor swaps a cure for a new treatment regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the verb LACE, as in lacing a drink; swap its C (hint of 'cure') for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a marked route that runners or swimmers must keep to, a set path.

clue.text: Habit formed by the taking of 15?

definitions.text: Habit formed by the taking of 15?

parts.words: Habit formed by the taking of 15?
parts.note: a custom built up by repeatedly taking particular remedies, read also as consumption of medicines

explanation.walkthrough: 15 is SPECIFICS, remedies for particular ailments; the word also means the act of using something, such as drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means customary practice, a habit, and also the act of consuming something.

clue.text: Focused on a wound finally medicated

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word wound is used

parts.note: dressed means treated with medicine and a bandage, as a wound is

explanation.surface: A nurse concentrates on a wound she has just treated.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to turn your attention to it, to concentrate on it.

clue.text: They're clearly defined and just what the doctor ordered

definitions.meaning: remedies aimed at a particular disease

explanation.definitionFit: Specifics are precise details, and in old medicine they were remedies for particular illnesses.

clue.text: Tense operation over in small theatre unit

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece sits inside the word for small

parts.note: slight means small or slender

indicators.note: over means the joined pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense surgery is completed in a small operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns T + OP round to POT, and 'in' places it inside SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotlight is a lamp in a stage lighting rig casting a narrow beam on performers.

clue.text: First left, then you'll see ENT sign

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: Hospital directions: turn left first, then follow the sign to ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen, a sign of something to come.

clue.text: E.g. State Registered Nurse is qualified for an opening

indicators.note: qualified suggests something modified or altered, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
SRN is the old British abbreviation for State Registered Nurse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A registered nurse is qualified to fill a job vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualified' looks like the nurse's credentials; it is the signal to rearrange EG, SRN and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a way in, an entrance.

clue.text: Hospital transplants originally involving one organ for another

indicators.note: involving means the outer pieces surround the inner one

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the word transplants is used

parts.note: the ear is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A hospital swaps one organ for another in a transplant operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts EAR inside H and T (from 'transplants originally').
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is a further organ beyond the ear already named in the clue.

clue.text: Man felt poorly — orally treated

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald

indicators.note: orally signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: ailed means felt unwell

explanation.surface: A sick man is given his medicine by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' looks medical but means entertained. 'orally' makes AILED sound like ALED.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain them lavishly, to treat them to food or stories.

clue.text: Jabbed without resistance with one of the 15?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for jabbed wraps round the letter

parts.note: dug means jabbed or poked, as in digging someone in the ribs
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A patient was injected without putting up a fight, with a specific remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside: DUG goes round R. 15 is SPECIFICS, remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific is a medicine for a particular ailment, and a drug is such a medicine.

clue.text: Appearance in London hospital by Speaker?

indicators.note: by Speaker signals that a word is to be heard spoken aloud rather than read

parts.note: Guy's is a famous teaching hospital in London

explanation.surface: An MP makes a showing at a London hospital alongside the Commons Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a major London hospital; its name sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or look, often a false one.

clue.text: Rallies -showing effects of stitches

definitions.meaning: in sewing, fabric drawn into small folds by a running thread

explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings are meetings of people, and in needlework the puckers made by drawing up a thread.

clue.text: Woman with NHS, losing 19, quits

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: 19 is HEART, so losing its heart means the middle letter goes and only the outer ones stay

explanation.surface: A woman leaves the health service after losing heart.
explanation.walkthrough: NHS is Britain's National Health Service; 19 is HEART, so 'losing 19' removes its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means being level with no debt either way, which is what evens means.

clue.text: Careful treatment's 'needed for ear I belted

indicators.note: treatment suggests something being worked on and handled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient who hit their ear needs gentle care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment's' signals a rearrangement of EAR I BELTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate means done with care and thought, not hasty.

clue.text: Maladies and Remedies (with page missing)

indicators.note: missing means the letter for page is taken away

parts.note: pills are medicinal tablets

explanation.surface: A list of diseases and cures, with one page torn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are troubles or sicknesses.

clue.text: Directs animal surgery's inauguration

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull

indicators.note: inauguration means the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A vet leads the opening of a new animal surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer something is to guide it, to direct it.

clue.text: Feverish disease with temperature in part of NY

indicators.note: in means the letter for temperature goes inside the rearranged letters
feverish suggests agitated and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A New York district suffers an outbreak of fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feverish' rearranges DISEASE, and 'in' places T among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Side is a district of Manhattan in New York City.
